_comment: Page copy for /g/uk-law-firms: the solicitors brief of 16 Oct 2026 (section 4) with the answers in the work document of 18 Oct 2026 (L1 to L36, F1 to F15) and the owner's decisions of 20 Oct 2026: no case cards until the four firms' figures and permissions are in (L6 fallback wording), payment version A (commission on new instructions), no register check. {THRESHOLD}, {OFFER} and {WORTH} are filled from config.json at build time. The build refuses dashes, exclamation marks, American spellings and a commission rate (see scripts/build-g-growth.mjs). Changed 26 Oct 2026 by the owner (workshop with Sondre, the new lead rules): fit.yes[0], fit.no[2] and outcomes.not-a-fit.p drop the two years of trading, and say that firms from £1m, or smaller firms with £2,000 a month for advertising, qualify.

meta.title: Elevate Marketing for UK law firms
meta.description: New instructions for UK law firms from campaigns we run. A few questions to see whether we would take you on.

topline: For law firms in England and Wales with {THRESHOLD}+ turnover
cta: See whether we would take you on

hero.h1a: We run client acquisition for law firms.

ingress.t: Our team has run client acquisition for four law and advisory firms in Norway. Different market, same mechanism:
a clear practice area, a clear offer
, and enquiries your fee earners actually want to take.

hero.micro: A few questions. We only take on firms we think we can help.

how.h2: One practice area at a time, tracked to instructions.
how.intro: A firm that wants more family work does not need more traffic. It needs the people who are searching for a family solicitor this week, a page that answers what they are asking, and a fee earner who calls back the same day. That is the whole mechanism, and it is the same in Bergen and Birmingham. What differs is regulation, competition and cost per click.

items.p: We start with one area where you have capacity and a named fee earner. Campaigns, pages and the follow-up are written for that work and nothing else.
Every enquiry is checked against the criteria we agree in advance before it reaches your inbox. Volume is not the aim. Instructions are.
You tell us each month which enquiries became instructions, from your own case management system. That count is what we are judged on and what we invoice on.

fit.h2: For firms that are growing, not firms that are stuck.
fit.body: The firms we work best with already win work through reputation and referral. What they lack is a second channel they control: enquiries that arrive because the right page was in front of the right person, in a practice area they want to grow.
yes: You are a firm in England and Wales with £1m or more in turnover, or a smaller firm that can put £2,000 a month into advertising
You act for private clients or businesses in areas such as family, conveyancing, wills and probate, employment, commercial or immigration
A new client is worth {WORTH} or more to you in the first year
Someone at the firm can respond to a new enquiry within one working day
no: Your work is mainly personal injury
Your work is mainly legal aid
You turn over less than £1m and cannot put £2,000 a month into advertising
Nobody has time to approve marketing material
fit.note: We check the details you give after you apply, and we confirm turnover with you on the call.

pay.h2: Paid when a new client instructs you. Our incentives are the same as yours.
pay.body: No retainer, no setup fee, no minimum term. We invoice a commission on new instructions that come from campaigns we run. The rate depends on what a client is worth to you, so we agree it before anything runs, in writing, so you can show the terms to your regulator and, where the rules require it, to your clients. It is not published, because it is not the same for two firms.
open: A new instruction is a new client who has formally instructed the firm, from an enquiry that came from a campaign we run. Existing clients and clients from other sources do not count. Personal injury matters never count.

The firm confirms each month which new instructions came from our campaigns, from its own case management records. We need a count and the agreed basis for the commission, not client names or matter details.
We invoice monthly, for instructions confirmed that month. Payment terms are 14 days.
If nothing is instructed, we invoice nothing.
The advertising budget is separate. You pay it to the platforms directly, and we agree it with you before anything runs.

items.p: A named solicitor at your firm signs off every ad and every page before it goes live. Text and images that the platforms generate on their own are switched off.
We work with enquiry numbers and outcomes. We never ask for, receive or store anything about a client's matter.
Campaigns run in ad accounts you own, tracked in your own systems. If we stop, you keep everything.

rows.status: What we judge ourselves on, and what we are paid on

meeting.body: We do not pitch. We sit down with your numbers and work out which practice area has the most headroom.

steps.p: You tell us your turnover, your main practice areas, your growth target for next year, and what a typical new instruction is worth.
We look at which practice area has the most headroom and what it would take to bring in more of that work.
You receive a one page sheet: new instructions per month needed to reach your target, and the enquiries that requires.

meeting.closing: You keep the sheet whether or not we work together. It contains your numbers only. No quote, no commission rate, no promise.

items.q: Your experience is Norwegian. Why would this work here?
items.a: The mechanism is the same: a clear practice area, a clear offer, and enquiries your fee earners want to take. What differs is regulation, competition and cost per click, and we go through those on the first call.
No. We advertise your firm. You decide which clients to take on, and we do not choose or recommend a solicitor. What we charge is set out in a written agreement that you can show your regulator.
A named solicitor at your firm. Nothing runs without that sign-off.
No. We can show you what we have done and how. We cannot promise a number of enquiries or instructions.

items.q: What do you need from us?
items.a: Access to your ad accounts, a way to tell which enquiries become instructions (if you do not have one yet, we set one up with you), and about an hour with whoever runs the practice area.

items.q: What if we want to stop?
items.a: There is no minimum term. You can stop with 30 days' notice, and you keep the accounts and the data.

footer.text: Elevate Marketing is operated by EngeCo AS, Norwegian organisation no. 924 490 926, Midtfjellet 66, 5363 Ågotnes, Norway.

consent.text: We use a Meta cookie to measure whether our advertising works. It is not set until you choose. The page works the same either way.

form.heading: See whether we would take you on
form.under: A few questions. We only take on firms we think we can help.
form.cta: See whether we would take you on
form.sending: Checking a few details. This takes a few seconds.
form.failed: Something went wrong on our side. Your answers are still here. Please try again, or email
form.consent: We use your details to reply to this application, to arrange a call and to keep a record of it. We contact you by email, and by text message if you give us a mobile number.

book.h: Thank you. Choose a time that suits you.
book.p: Pick a slot for a {OFFER}. Your own numbers are all we need.
book.small: No time that works? Reply to the confirmation email and we will find one.

takk.p: We will send a confirmation and a short note on what to have to hand: last year's turnover, your main practice areas, your growth target for next year, and what a typical new instruction is worth to the firm.

review.h: Thank you. We will be in touch within one working day.
review.p: We want to check a few details before we suggest a time.

not-now.h: Thank you. Come back when you have capacity.
not-now.p: If you are at capacity now, we will ask again in three months.

not-a-fit.h: Thank you. This is not the right fit at the moment.
not-a-fit.p: We work with firms in England and Wales outside personal injury that turn over £1m or more, and with smaller firms that can put £2,000 a month into advertising. If that changes, we would be glad to hear from you.
not-a-fit.note: If we have misread your answers, email {EMAIL} and we will look again.

interest.h: Looking for a new website instead?
interest.p: If you would like a fixed-price quote for a new website, or a monthly retainer for your marketing, press the button and we will email you once, within two working days. A person at Elevate Marketing also reads every application, and may email you once about this if we think it could suit your firm. Every email says how to say no.
interest.done: Thank you. We will email you from {EMAIL} within two working days.
interest.error: That did not go through. Email {EMAIL} and ask for a quote, and we will send one.
interest.noscript: To ask for a quote on a new website, email {EMAIL}.
